Amy (Sales): Heads-up — ACME demo just hit repeated 5xxs and capacity throttling around 15:34 PT. Demo paused. Can someone triage? /cc Ravi
Ravi (Solutions): On it. Please paste any sample logs or request IDs and the route/model. :eyes:
Amy (Sales): route=prod-acme, model=redwood-stable-7b, region=us-west-2. Getting lots of 503 and a few 504s. Sample curl client output:
Amy (Sales): ```
HTTP/1.1 503 Service Unavailable
x-request-id: req_abc123
content-type: application/json
{"error":"server overloaded, try again"}
```
Noah (Oncall): I'm oncall — I see autoscale events coincident with the spike. Pulling runtime logs now.
deploy-bot: ```
[15:33:45] event=burstpool.scale_start pool=burstpool route=prod-acme
[15:34:10] event=burstpool.scale_complete pool=burstpool size=2->6
[15:34:40] event=request.error route=prod-acme code=503 spike=120rps
[15:35:05] event=fallback route=prod-acme -> prod-acme-quantized
```
Sasha (Runtime): Looks like burstpool attach latency (~20–30s) created a transient under-provision. Warm pools would prevent this. Temporary mitigations: 1) enable immediate fallback to quantized variant, 2) reduce client concurrency, 3) increase burstpool min for this route.
Ravi (Solutions): Can we flip the fallback and ask the client to throttle concurrency from 8 -> 2 for the live demo? Amy, can they do that?
Amy (Sales): They can drop to 2 now. Please flip fallback. Also they're asking about short-term Dedicated/committed pricing for demos — what's the minimum? :moneybag:
Ravi (Solutions): Minimum demo commit we can fast-track is 2 GPUs for the month via our Partner demo program (needs sales OK). I'll loop in Jordan on pricing after triage.
Noah (Oncall): Fallback enabled to redwood-stable-7b-quant. Error rate trending down; 200s returning. Watching for new spikes.
Amy (Sales): Confirmed client seeing 200s, demo resumed. Thank you.
Sasha (Runtime): Preventative action items: 1) document pre-warm steps / reserved/demo pool 2) tweak autoscale policy for faster attach on demo routes (reduce attach backoff) 3) add client-side concurrency limit + exponential backoff in quickstart 4) postmortem if this breaches SLA or recurs.
Ravi (Solutions): I'll draft a one-page runbook (how to pre-warm, when to request reserved capacity, quick CLI toggles for fallback) and a short blurb for the pricing FAQ re: demo commits.
Amy (Sales): Great — ping me the runbook link when ready and I'll share with the customer. Thanks everyone! :thumbsup:
